title: No refund ceiling: total gateway refunds for a booking can exceed what was captured, without limit
actor: Two staff actors, both real platform roles, both forwarded-identity authenticated (oai-authenticated-user-email header, rows in app_users, status=active). (1) ops.admin@pawspace.test, role_code=admin, holds communications.message — files the refund cases. (2) finance.mgr@pawspace.test, role_code=finance, holds payments.manage — sends them to the gateway. Not preview. A single admin can also do both halves: admin holds neither payments.manage nor is it required to, but the two roles together are the ordinary refund workflow.
request:
Loop, three times, on ONE booking BK-1 whose captured value is Rs 8,000:
  POST /api/booking-operations {action:"refund_requested",bookingId:"BK-1",providerId:"PRV-1",reason:"refund attempt number N"}   (app/api/booking-operations/route.ts POST, line 292-295)
  POST /api/grooming-payment-sandbox {action:"initiate_refund",bookingId:"BK-1"}                             (app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox/route.ts POST, line 22-27)
response: All six calls succeeded. refund_requested -> 201 {data:{refundCaseId:"4a06be0d-..."}} / 201 {..."2a45a64d-..."} / 201 {..."ba1f558f-..."}. initiate_refund -> 201 {"data":{"bookingId":"BK-1","refundCaseId":"4a06be0d-...","gatewayRefundId":"rfnd_1","status":"processed","environment":"sandbox"}} and the same shape for rfnd_2 and rfnd_3.
d1_after: booking_refund_cases: three rows, each amount=8000, status='processing', gateway_reference='rfnd_1'/'rfnd_2'/'rfnd_3'. Three DISTINCT outbound calls were made to POST https://api.razorpay.com/v1/payments/pay_REAL1/refund, each body {amount:800000} (Rs 8,000), each carrying a DIFFERENT X-Refund-Idempotency header (the refund case UUID), so the gateway's own idempotency cannot collapse them. Rs 24,000 of refund instructions against Rs 8,000 collected. Nothing in the request path compared the running refund total to captured_amount, to booking_payments.amount, or to the sum of prior refund cases.
repeatable: Yes. Run twice, identical outcome both times; the loop is itself the second and third repetition. The ceiling is absent, not racy — no interleaving is required and adding more iterations adds Rs 8,000 of refund each time without bound.
canonical_failure: No code path caps the sum of a booking's refunds at the amount actually captured, so N internal refund cases produce N full-value gateway refunds against a single capture.
money_consequence: Exact rupee consequence per iteration: Rs 8,000 leaves the merchant account that never arrived. Three iterations on one Rs 8,000 booking sent Rs 24,000, a net loss of Rs 16,000. The loop is unbounded — the only limit is the balance in the Razorpay account.
blast_radius: Every booking with a captured payment, every service line (the same booking_refund_cases table and the same grooming-payment-sandbox refund endpoint serve grooming, sitting, training, taxi, walking, boarding and food). Any admin/manager (communications.message) plus any finance user (payments.manage) — or one person holding a role with both. Also corrupts finance reporting: lib/unit-economics.ts counts only status='processed' cases, so these three Rs 8,000 real refunds report as Rs 0 of refund.
evidence_path: scratchpad/p/p3-refund-money-out.mjs (real route handlers; only globalThis.fetch was stubbed to observe the outbound gateway calls without contacting Razorpay)
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-01: a booking cannot refund more than it collected" + "W2-PAY-01: a PARTIAL refund still works, and the remainder is still refundable"
fix_note: A gateway refund is refused when prior approved/processing/processed/completed refunds plus this one would exceed the amount actually captured (409 refund_exceeds_capture). Partial refunds and the remaining headroom are unaffected.

title: initiate_refund sends money to the gateway for a refund case that was never approved — its own error text claims otherwise
actor: finance.mgr@pawspace.test, role_code=finance, permission payments.manage, forwarded-identity staff actor, not preview.
request: POST /api/grooming-payment-sandbox {action:"initiate_refund",bookingId:"BK-1"} where the only booking_refund_cases row has status='requested' and approved_by=NULL.
d1_after: booking_refund_cases: {status:'processing',gateway_reference:'rfnd_1'}; one real POST to https://api.razorpay.com/v1/payments/pay_REAL1/refund for {amount:800000}. The refund_status approval ladder in app/api/booking-operations/route.ts (requested -> approved -> processing -> completed) was never entered; segregation of duties never applied.
repeatable: Yes, ran three times in the same probe with three separate unapproved cases; every one reached the gateway.
canonical_failure: app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox/route.ts line 25 selects the latest booking_refund_cases row and only refuses status='processed', so a case in the initial 'requested' state is paid out while the endpoint returns the message "Create and approve an internal refund case before gateway refund" for the no-case case only.
money_consequence: The full refund case amount (Rs 8,000 in the probe; in production the whole booking_payments.amount, since app/api/booking-operations/route.ts line 294 seeds the case at Number(payment?.amount ?? 0)) leaves the merchant account on the say-so of one finance user with no second approver and no maker-checker record.
blast_radius: Every refundable booking. Removes the entire approval ladder from the money-moving path; combined with W2-07-PAY-001 it is a single-actor unbounded drain if one role holds both permissions.
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-02: money does not move for a refund case nobody approved"
fix_note: initiate_refund refuses any case whose status is not 'approved' (409 refund_not_approved) before it reaches the gateway boundary. The test counts gateway refund instructions, so it measures money that would have left, not just the response code.

title: PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV unset defaults to sandbox, leaving the staff gateway-event simulator open — staff can record a Rs 8,000 capture with zero gateway contact
actor: finance.mgr@pawspace.test, role_code=finance, permission payments.manage, forwarded-identity staff actor, not preview.
d1_after: booking_payments: {status:'captured',gateway:'razorpay_sandbox'}. payment_reconciliation_records: {expected_amount:8000,captured_amount:8000,refunded_amount:0,gateway_status:'captured',reconciliation_status:'matched'}. Outbound fetch calls to any gateway during both requests: 0 (counted at globalThis.fetch). No signature was verified because processGatewayEvent was handed signatureVerified:true by the route itself (app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox/route.ts line 35).
repeatable: Yes, ran twice (probes p2-routes.mjs and p3-refund-money-out.mjs), identical result.
canonical_failure: app/api/grooming-payment-sandbox/route.ts line 13 gates the whole simulator on String(runtime.PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV||"sandbox").toLowerCase()!=="sandbox", so an ABSENT or empty variable resolves to "sandbox" and unlocks a staff endpoint that writes signatureVerified:true gateway events for any booking at any amount.
money_consequence: A booking becomes financially 'captured' for its full value with no money received — Rs 8,000 per call in the probe, and the amount is caller-supplied (input.amount) so any figure is accepted. Downstream this makes provider_settlement_readiness eligible (grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts, the collectedInFull branch), so PawSpace pays the provider's settlement out of its own funds for a service the customer never paid for; it also creates the pay_* reference that W2-07-PAY-001's refund path needs, letting the same staff pair refund money that was never collected.
blast_radius: Any deployment where PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV is not explicitly set — the fail-closed default the module documents is fail-OPEN for this route. Same fallback appears in lib/razorpay-client.ts paymentEnvironment (String(env?.PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_ENV || "sandbox")) and lib/payment-webhook-gate.ts paymentMode, so an unset variable also silently selects the sandbox webhook secret and stamps every live event environment="sandbox".

title: Refund webhook attributes every gateway refund to the newest refund case: refunded_amount reached Rs 24,000 against Rs 8,000 captured, and two cases were left stranded
actor: The Razorpay webhook receiver itself (lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts processGatewayEvent), driven directly with three signature-verified refund.processed events — exactly what the gateway sends after the three real refunds proved in W2-07-PAY-001.
request: processGatewayEvent(db, {provider:'razorpay',environment:'sandbox',eventId:'evt_rf_1'|'evt_rf_2'|'evt_rf_3', eventType:'refund.processed', bookingId:'BK-1', gatewayPaymentId:'pay_REAL1', gatewayRefundId:'rfnd_A'|'rfnd_B'|'rfnd_C', amountSubunits:800000, currency:'INR', signatureVerified:true}) — three separate event ids, three separate gateway refund ids.
response: {duplicate:false,status:'processed',bookingId:'BK-1',paymentId:'PAY-BK-1'} for all three. None returned an error or a refusal.
d1_before: payment_reconciliation_records: {expected_amount:8000,captured_amount:8000,refunded_amount:0,gateway_status:'captured'}. booking_refund_cases: RC-1, RC-2, RC-3, each amount=8000, status='requested'.
d1_after: payment_reconciliation_records: {expected_amount:8000,captured_amount:8000,refunded_amount:24000,gateway_status:'refunded',reconciliation_status:'refund_overage',variance_amount:16000}. booking_payments: {status:'refunded'}. booking_refund_cases: RC-1 status='requested' (untouched), RC-2 status='requested' (untouched), RC-3 status='processed' gateway_reference='rfnd_C' (rewritten three times). payment_reconciliation_exceptions: two rows exception_type='refund_overage', severity='critical', status='open'.
repeatable: Yes, ran twice with identical numbers.
canonical_failure: lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts line 243 resolves the refund case with "SELECT * FROM booking_refund_cases WHERE booking_id=? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1" instead of matching on the gateway refund id, so every refund on a booking is booked against the newest case and refunded_amount accumulates past captured_amount with only a post-hoc exception.
money_consequence: Rs 24,000 recorded as refunded against Rs 8,000 collected — a Rs 16,000 hole that the ledger itself reports as variance_amount:16000 AFTER the money moved rather than refusing it. The refund_overage branch (line 253) raises an exception but still commits the refund and still flips booking_payments to 'refunded'; it is a report, not a control.
blast_radius: Any booking with more than one refund case, which W2-07-PAY-001 shows any admin can create at will. Also silently strands genuine refund cases: RC-1 and RC-2 stayed 'requested' forever even though their money was refunded at the gateway, so the ops work queue (lib/ops-work-queue.ts, status='requested' -> finance) shows two open refunds that were already paid, inviting a fourth and fifth payout.
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-06: each gateway refund settles its OWN refund case, and none is left stranded" + "W2-PAY-06: an event names its own case even when a newer one exists, and a redelivery claims nothing"
fix_note: A gateway refund now settles the case it belongs to: the case carrying that gateway refund id is authoritative, and only on an event's first contact does the newest case take it - excluding any case already claimed by a DIFFERENT gateway refund. Ordering and the orphan_gateway_refund fallback are unchanged. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: refunded_amount still accumulates past captured_amount and still raises refund_overage rather than refusing. By the time refund.processed arrives the money has already left at the gateway, so a receiver that declined to record it would make the ledger lie in the other direction; the control belongs at initiation and is W2-07-PAY-001.

title: Money collected on one customer's order settles a different customer's booking: the gateway order id is never checked against the booking the payload names
actor: Whoever populates payment.notes on the Razorpay payment entity. lib/razorpay-client.ts sets notes only on the ORDER; app/api/razorpay-webhook/route.ts extract() reads payment.notes FIRST and falls back to order.notes, so the payment-entity notes (which Razorpay Checkout accepts from the client that opens checkout) win. The event is fully signature-verified — this is not a forgery, it is a trusted field that is never cross-checked.
request:
POST /api/razorpay-webhook with a correctly HMAC-SHA256-signed body:
{event:"payment.captured",created_at:...,payload:{payment:{entity:{id:"pay_1",order_id:"order_A",amount:800000,currency:"INR",notes:{booking_id:"BK-B"}}}}}
headers x-razorpay-signature=<valid>, x-razorpay-event-id=evt_m1.
order_A is the order lib/payment-order-intent.ts opened for BK-A (customer CUS-1, Rs 8,000). BK-B belongs to CUS-2 and has NO gateway order of its own.
response: 200 {"ok":true,"environment":"sandbox","duplicate":false,"status":"processed","bookingId":"BK-B","paymentId":"PAY-BK-B"} — the receiver itself reports it settled BK-B.
d1_before: booking_payments: BK-A/CUS-1 amount 8000 status 'awaiting_payment'; BK-B/CUS-2 amount 8000 status 'awaiting_payment'. payment_gateway_links: one row {booking_id:'BK-A',gateway_order_id:'order_A',gateway_payment_id:NULL}. payment_reconciliation_records: {payment_id:'PAY-BK-A',expected_amount:8000,captured_amount:0,gateway_status:'order_linked'}. provider_settlement_readiness: {booking_id:'BK-B',payout_amount:5600,status:'awaiting_payment_verification'}.
d1_after: booking_payments: BK-A still 'awaiting_payment'; BK-B now 'captured'. payment_reconciliation_records: PAY-BK-A {captured_amount:0,gateway_status:'order_linked',reconciliation_status:'pending'} and a NEW row PAY-BK-B {expected_amount:8000,captured_amount:8000,gateway_status:'captured',reconciliation_status:'matched'}. provider_settlement_readiness BK-B -> status:'eligible' (Rs 5,600 released to BK-B's provider). payment_gateway_links: still only the BK-A row — BK-B was settled with no gateway link at all. payment_reconciliation_exceptions: EMPTY. Nothing anywhere records that the money belonged to order_A.
repeatable: Yes, ran twice (p4-webhook.mjs T5 and p5-binding.mjs M1), identical result both times.
canonical_failure: lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts resolvePayment (line 141) resolves the booking from event.bookingId (the payload's notes) BEFORE it ever looks at payment_gateway_links, and never verifies that the gateway order id the money was collected against belongs to the booking it is about to settle.
money_consequence: Rs 8,000 collected from CUS-1 was applied to CUS-2's booking. CUS-2 receives a Rs 8,000 service free, CUS-2's provider is paid Rs 5,600 of settlement out of it, and CUS-1's booking stays unpaid — so CUS-1 is re-chased or re-charged Rs 8,000 for a payment they already made. Net exposure per event: Rs 8,000 misapplied plus Rs 5,600 paid out, with a Rs 8,000 double-charge risk.
blast_radius: Every booking whose booking_payments.amount equals the paid amount. BOUNDED, measured: a redirect to a Rs 20,000 booking with a Rs 8,000 payment IS refused (200 {status:'exception',reason:'capture_amount_mismatch'}, booking untouched) because expected falls back to booking_payments.amount when the target has no linked order — so the hijack works only between equal-priced bookings, which for a standard-price package is most of them.
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-03: a payment cannot settle a booking its gateway order was not opened for" + "W2-PAY-03: the booking the order WAS opened for still settles normally"
fix_note: processGatewayEvent now refuses an event whose payload names a booking different from the booking that payment_gateway_links records the named gateway order / payment-link / payment reference was opened for (exception gateway_order_booking_mismatch, reconciliation exception raised against the RIGHTFUL booking). No new matching rule was invented: a payload note simply stops outranking the platform's own link record. An identifier the platform has no link for still decides nothing, and an event carrying no gateway reference is untouched.

title: Replaying a REFUSED gateway event grants the entitlement it was refused for: a Rs 1 payment activates a Rs 24,000 ten-session subscription
actor: Anyone able to re-send a previously delivered, signature-valid webhook body: the gateway's own delivery retry, an operator clicking 'resend' in the Razorpay dashboard, or any holder of one captured signed request. The receiver enforces NO replay window — payload.created_at is read only to stamp createdAt and is never compared to now, and there is no nonce or freshness check — so a signed body stays replayable forever.
request:
The SAME signed body posted twice to POST /api/razorpay-webhook, byte-identical, same x-razorpay-signature, same x-razorpay-event-id=evt_rz_1:
{event:"payment.captured",payload:{payment:{entity:{id:"pay_real",order_id:"order_real",amount:100,currency:"INR",notes:{booking_id:"BK-SUB"}}}}}  (amount 100 subunits = Rs 1 against a Rs 24,000 booking)
response: Delivery 1: 200 {"ok":true,"environment":"sandbox","duplicate":false,"status":"exception","reason":"capture_amount_mismatch"}. Delivery 2: 200 {"ok":true,"environment":"sandbox","duplicate":true,"status":"exception"} — it answers with the OLD refusal while performing a new, money-granting write.
d1_after:
After delivery 1: unchanged entitlement; payment_gateway_events {event_id:'evt_rz_1',booking_id:'BK-SUB',processing_status:'exception',failure_reason:'Capture amount mismatch'}; payment_reconciliation_exceptions {exception_type:'capture_amount_mismatch',detail:{expected:24000,received:1,variance:-23999}}.
After delivery 2: customer_grooming_subscriptions {status:'active',sessions_reserved:10}. booking_subscription_usage {status:'reserved',sessions_reserved:10}. booking_lifecycle_events {event_type:'subscription_activated',detail:{sessionsReserved:10,eventId:'evt_rz_1',verified:true}} — it stamps verified:true. booking_payments STILL {status:'awaiting_payment'}. payment_reconciliation_records {expected_amount:24000,captured_amount:1,gateway_status:'captured',reconciliation_status:'amount_mismatch'}.
repeatable: Yes, ran twice with identical output.
canonical_failure: lib/grooming-payment-reconciliation.ts processGatewayEvent's duplicate branch (line 147-160) calls activateSubscriptionOnCapture for any recorded event whose event_type is a capture type WITHOUT checking that event's processing_status, and lib/subscription-payment-activation.ts activateSubscriptionOnCapture never checks that a capture was actually reconciled — so replaying an event the system explicitly REFUSED grants the entitlement it refused.
money_consequence: Ten grooming sessions, immediately redeemable, on a Rs 1 payment: the plan's full value Rs 24,000 of service delivered for Re 1, plus the provider cost of ten visits. The recorded payment stays 'awaiting_payment', so finance sees an unpaid booking while the credits are live. This is the same PAY-002 defect the module's own header says it fixed — the purchase path was closed but the replay path was not.
blast_radius: Every subscription purchase booking sitting in pending_payment. The symmetrical branch is the same: replaying a refused payment.failed event calls failSubscriptionOnPaymentFailure and can close a genuinely paid entitlement. Because there is no replay window, the exposure does not expire.
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-04: replaying a REFUSED capture does not grant the entitlement it was refused for" + "W2-PAY-04: a redelivery of a genuinely PROCESSED capture still completes the entitlement"
fix_note: The duplicate-event repair path now runs only for a recorded event whose processing_status is 'processed'. Repair exists to complete a transition a transient dependent-write failure rolled back after an ACCEPTED capture; an event the system refused is not a transition waiting to be completed. Fails closed in both directions - a refused capture grants nothing, and a replayed refused payment.failed can no longer close a genuinely paid entitlement. The regression drives the real POST /api/razorpay-webhook with a real HMAC signature; its companion proves a genuinely processed capture's redelivery still completes and does not reserve sessions twice.

title: A replayed event id takes its booking from the NEW payload, so the same event id can act on a booking it never referred to
actor: Anyone who can send a signed webhook body twice with a changed notes.booking_id — a payload-substituting replay. The signature must be valid for each body, so this is the gateway-side or shared-secret-holder variant of W2-07-PAY-006, not an unauthenticated attack.
request:
POST /api/razorpay-webhook twice with x-razorpay-event-id=evt_replay both times.
Pass 1 body: payment.captured, {payment:{entity:{id:'pay_z',order_id:'order_NOWHERE',amount:100,currency:'INR'}}} — no notes at all, matches nothing.
Pass 2 body: the same event id, now {…,notes:{booking_id:'BK-SUB'}}.
d1_before: payment_gateway_events after pass 1: {event_id:'evt_replay',booking_id:NULL,processing_status:'exception'}. customer_grooming_subscriptions: {id:'SUB-1',source_booking_id:'BK-SUB',status:'pending_payment',sessions_reserved:0}. booking_payments BK-SUB: 'awaiting_payment'. payment_reconciliation_records: EMPTY.
d1_after: customer_grooming_subscriptions {status:'active',sessions_reserved:10}; booking_subscription_usage {status:'reserved',sessions_reserved:10}; booking_lifecycle_events {event_type:'subscription_activated',detail:{eventId:'evt_replay',verified:true}}. payment_gateway_events row UNCHANGED — still booking_id NULL, processing_status 'exception'. payment_reconciliation_records STILL EMPTY: not one rupee was ever reconciled for BK-SUB, and no audit row links evt_replay to BK-SUB.
canonical_failure: The duplicate branch computes repairBookingId as String(existing.booking_id||event.bookingId||""), so when the stored event has no booking the replayed payload's own notes.booking_id decides which booking gets acted on.
money_consequence: Rs 24,000 of subscription entitlement (10 sessions) activated against a booking the recorded event never referenced, leaving no forensic link between the event row and the booking it changed.
blast_radius: Any pending_payment entitlement can be targeted by reusing any event id already recorded with a NULL booking_id — and unmatched_gateway_event is the ordinary way an event gets recorded with a NULL booking_id, so such ids accumulate naturally in payment_gateway_events.
regression: tests/ptja-p1-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-PAY-05: a replayed event id cannot act on a booking the recorded event never referred to"
fix_note: Closed by the W2-07-PAY-006 processing_status gate (verified: the regression reproduces against the pre-fix commit and passes after), and the mechanism itself removed - the repair target is now taken strictly from the RECORDED event row, never from the replayed payload. A genuinely processed capture always has its booking stamped on the event row, so the removed fallback could only ever have fired for an event that had none.

title: REFUTATION: signature is verified before any state change, and an absent or whitespace-only signing secret fails closed
request: (a) A well-formed payment.captured body with x-razorpay-signature set to 64 zero bytes of hex. (b) The same body correctly signed, but with RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_SANDBOX set to the whitespace string "   ".
response: (a) 401 {"error":"Invalid Razorpay webhook signature"}. (b) 503 {"error":"Razorpay sandbox webhook secret is not configured (RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_SANDBOX)"}.
d1_before: payment_gateway_events: 0 rows. booking_payments: BK-A and BK-B both 'awaiting_payment'.
d1_after: IDENTICAL. payment_gateway_events: 0 rows. Both bookings still 'awaiting_payment'. No row was inserted before verification — the gate, the header check and the HMAC comparison all run before database() is even called, and the comparison is constant-time (safeEqual).
canonical_failure: None — this control is correctly ordered and fails closed. lib/payment-webhook-gate.ts trims the secret, so an empty or whitespace value is treated as absent rather than as a usable key, and live mode additionally requires PAWSPACE_PAYMENT_LIVE_APPROVED="true" plus a distinct RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_LIVE.
blast_radius: n/a — reported so this surface is not re-hunted.

title: REFUTATION: an equal event id replayed as a DIFFERENT event type does not re-run the money path
actor: Replayer holding a valid signature for each body.
request: POST /api/razorpay-webhook with x-razorpay-event-id=evt_1 first as payment.captured (Rs 8,000, order_A, BK-A), then the SAME event id as refund.processed {refund:{entity:{id:'rfnd_X',payment_id:'pay_1',amount:800000}}}.
d1_after: UNCHANGED for the money columns: refunded_amount stayed 0, booking_payments stayed 'captured', and the stored event row for evt_1 stayed event_type='payment.captured', amount_subunits=800000 — the second payload's type and amount were not written over it. The UNIQUE(provider,event_id) index plus the early duplicate return hold the capture/refund ledger.
canonical_failure: None for the ledger. NOTE the residual defect recorded separately as W2-07-PAY-006/007: the duplicate branch is not a pure no-op — it still runs the subscription repair, and that is where the replay damage lives.
